matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides, determine the numeric difference, and then search for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator to exactly offset that difference.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and you need a systematic way to find a single‑stick change that balances the numeric values.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without considering the numeric imbalance, leaving the equation still incorrect.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, relocate one of V’s diagonal sticks so that the two sticks intersect, turning V into X and increasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 5 and a V numeral is present.
matchstick.example: Attempting to convert V to X when the imbalance is not 5, which fails to fix the equation.

matchstick.title: Swap I and V in IV to make VI (adds 2)
matchstick.principle: When the imbalance is exactly 2 and the pattern IV appears, move the vertical stick of the I onto the V to form VI, increasing the value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 2 and the numeral IV is present.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to VI when the numeric difference is not 2, leaving the equation unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present and the equation can be fixed by decreasing the right‑hand side, move the vertical stick from the plus sign to a numeral (usually V or I) to turn + into – and simultaneously add an I, adjusting the values appropriately.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is too large and a plus sign exists.
matchstick.example: Changing + to – but not using the removed vertical stick to modify a numeral, so the numeric imbalance remains.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: When the equation is off by 1 and there are isolated I’s, relocate a vertical stick from one I to another numeral to increase one value by 1 and decrease the other by 1, achieving balance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric difference is 1 and at least two I’s are present.
matchstick.example: Moving an I stick when the imbalance is not 1, which fails to correct the equation.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign; never move its sticks
matchstick.principle: Never relocate any matchsticks that belong to the '=' sign; altering it would break the equality operator and invalidate the puzzle.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every problem; the equality sign must remain unchanged.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from the '=' sign to change a numeral, resulting in an invalid equality operator.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: If a minus sign appears and the numeric imbalance is large, move a horizontal stick from a numeral onto the minus sign to create a second horizontal line, turning it into an '=' sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a minus sign and the RHS needs to become equal to the LHS.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn – into = without a spare horizontal stick, leaving the operator malformed.

matchstick.title: Relocate minus sign to a different position
matchstick.principle: When a minus sign is present, consider moving its single horizontal stick to a new location in the equation (e.g., from the RHS to between the LHS terms) to change the arithmetic structure and achieve balance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation is false and a minus sign exists, try moving the minus sign rather than altering only numerals.
matchstick.example: Keeping the minus sign in its original place and only modifying numerals, which fails to find a solution.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: If you need to change a minus sign into a plus sign, you must also relocate a vertical stick from a numeral to the operator, because a plus sign requires both a horizontal and a vertical stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution requires turning – into +, ensure you also supply the missing vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Changing – to + without adding a vertical stick, leaving the plus sign incomplete.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the equality sign as just another collection of sticks and tries to use its sticks to adjust numerals, forgetting that the operator must stay intact.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select any stick that belongs to the '=' sign for relocation; keep the equality operator unchanged.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes forgets to include all original symbols after the transformation, resulting in a malformed equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, rewrite the entire equation, ensuring every numeral and operator from the original appears (except the moved stick, which is placed elsewhere).

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick (resulting in an incomplete plus sign)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes that replacing the horizontal line of – with + is enough, overlooking that a plus sign also needs a vertical stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting – to +, also relocate a vertical stick from a numeral to the operator so that the plus sign consists of both a horizontal and a vertical stick.
